dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Functional (psychogenic) neurological disorder presenting as a cerebellar-type syndrome with head titubation, gait unsteadiness, and dysarthria

Alternatives I would still consider:
1. Multiple system atrophy, cerebellar type (MSA-C) – would expect progressive course, autonomic features, and MRI signs of pontocerebellar atrophy (absent here, but cannot be fully excluded at this stage)
2. Essential tremor with prominent head (and possible voice) involvement – less likely given absence of upper-limb action tremor and lack of chronic progression
3. Idiopathic late-onset cerebellar ataxia – usually slowly progressive, with cerebellar atrophy on MRI, neither of which is present
